overview.description: Hearts variant: matching cards in a trick cancel (no points). Different scoring from base Hearts.

history.origins: Hearts first appeared at the end of the nineteenth century and is popular in many countries. Cancellation Hearts is an American variant for six to ten players using two 52-card packs shuffled together; when identical cards are played to the same trick they cancel each other for trick-taking but still carry penalty points if they are hearts or the Queen of Spades.
timeline: 20th century: Hearts variant with cancellation rule documented; played in USA.

nullReasons.evolution: No documented evolution; standard Hearts variant with cancellation rule.
nullReasons.cultural: Played as Hearts variant in USA; no distinct cultural doc.

setup.players: Cancellation Hearts is commonly played by six to ten players; this build uses four players with one deck. No partnerships; play is clockwise.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. The classic Cancellation form uses two 52-card packs shuffled together for six to ten players; this entry uses one pack for four players.
setup.dealing: All cards are dealt out as far as they go; any leftover go to a face-down kitty taken by the winner of the first trick. For 4 players, 13 cards each, one at a time. After the deal, pass three cards (left, right, across, no pass by round).

rules.objective: Avoid scoring penalty points. Achieve the lowest total score; when two identical cards are played to a trick they cancel each other for trick-taking (no winner from that pair) but still carry penalty points if they are hearts or the Queen of Spades.
rules.gameplay: Standard Hearts: 13 each; pass 3; 2♣ leads; must follow suit. Matching cards in a trick cancel each other (no points). Queen of Spades 13; each heart 1. Shoot moon = 0 or pass 26 to others. Lowest score wins.

phases.label: Trick Play
phases.notes: Players play one card per turn. Lowest card leads first trick. Follow suit if possible; otherwise any card. Trick won by highest card of led suit. Trick winner leads next.

phases.label: Round End
phases.notes: Score points for hearts (1 pt each) and Queen of Spades (13 pts). Matching cards cancel that trick's points.

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card deck is used, with no jokers. All fifty-two cards are dealt. In Cancellation Hearts, matching cards played to the same trick cancel each other for the purpose of determining the trick winner.
engine.suitDescription: The four French suits are Spades, Hearts, Diamonds, and Clubs. There is no trump suit; all suits are equal for following. Hearts remain the penalty suit; the Queen of Spades carries a high penalty.
engine.rankDescription: Standard ranks from Ace (high) down to two (low) in each suit. The highest card of the suit led wins the trick unless cancelled by an identical card; there are thirteen ranks per suit.

synthesis.shortDescription: A Hearts variant where identical cards played in the same trick cancel out, preventing points from being scored.

prompts.human: Welcome to Cancellation Hearts. Play to avoid taking hearts and the Queen of Spades. But here's the twist: if two identical cards are played in the same trick, they cancel each other and no points are scored. Strategy involves predicting what cards others will play and matching them when possible.
prompts.ai: Game: Cancellation Hearts (Hearts variant). Setup: 4 players, 52-card deck, 13 cards dealt per player. Turn sequence: Players play one card per trick in clockwise order. Lead card determines suit. Follow suit if able; else any card. Highest led-suit card wins trick. Cancellation: identical cards in same trick = 0 points. Scoring: Hearts 1pt each, Queen of Spades 13pts. Win: Lowest total score.

scoring.description: Points scored by taking heart cards and the Queen of Spades. Matching cards in a trick cancel (zero points for that trick).
scoring.winCondition: Lowest cumulative score after all rounds wins.
